instructions: Drain and rinse the black-eyed peas and leave them in the colander. Peel the carrot and slice it into thin rounds. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat 3 tbsp of the olive oil in a wide, deep pot over medium-high heat. Add the onion and 1/2 tsp of the salt and cook for 6 minutes, until soft and see-through.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Turn the heat to low, add the tomato paste, and stir for 1 minute, scraping the bottom of the pot.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and 1 cup water. Add the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper. Turn the heat to high and bring it to a boil.
Add the spinach in handfuls and toss until it starts to wilt, about 3 minutes. Add the carrot slices and the black-eyed peas and toss to combine.
Turn the heat to very low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Stir gently halfway through. The carrot should be tender when you pierce it with a fork.
Take the pot off the heat. Juice 1 lemon and stir in 3 tbsp of the juice. Chop 2 tbsp of the dill and stir it in with the remaining olive oil. Cut the second lemon in half.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lemon.
Serve hot with the lemon halves.
method_notes: No version has 20 ratings and RecipeTin Eats has none, so the lead is Greek Cooking Made Easy's tomato yiahni, which is vegan and Lenten: onion, tomato paste and tomato simmered with spinach, carrot and black-eyed peas, then finished with olive oil, lemon and dill. Lemon and Olives agrees on the tomato, spinach and peas but uses oregano and thyme instead of dill and simmers dried peas for 45 minutes. Canned peas replace the lead's dried peas, which need a 25 to 30 minute parboil, so the dish takes 40 minutes in all.
